simple.meaning: בְּדֹלַח (bᵉdôlach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something in pieces , i.e. bdellium , a (fragrant) gum (perhaps amber); others a pearl.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 2:12. The surrounding context includes land.

definitions.short: something in pieces , i.e. bdellium , a (fragrant) gum (perhaps amber); others a pearl
definitions.full: H916. bedolach בְּדֹ֫לַח noun [masculine] probably bdellium ( ᵑ6 ; בְּדוּלְחָא ᵑ7 ; etymology dubious; Lag Ges. Abh. 20 proposes Sanskrit udûkhala ) with article ׳הַבְּ , apparently therefore well known; one of the products of the land Havilah Gen 2:12 ; used in simile of colour of manna הַבְּדֹלַח כְּעֵין וְעֵינוֺ Num 11:7 . — Meaning somewhat uncertain; ᵐ5 Gen 2:12 ἄνθραξ , Num 11:7 κρύσταλλος ; Saad AW Ki Bo and others pearls , compare Lag Or. ii. 44; Jos Ant. iii. 1 . 6 Aq Theod Symm ᵑ7 most bdellium , an odoriferous transparent gum, of yellowish colour. (compare Smith Dict. Bible Sigismund Aromata, 18 .)

occurrences.englishText: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium† or, aromatic resin and onyx stone are also there.
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.† Bdellium is a resin extracted from certain African trees.
